newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CONSENSUS-Reuters survey of NZ economic forecasts.
newsitem.headline: CONSENSUS-Reuters survey of NZ economic forecasts.

text.p: The following New Zealand economic indicators are scheduled for release on Thursday this week. Times are GMT. Average forecasts for the Reserve Bank of New Zealand's June Monetary Policy Statement, due on Friday, will be released on Tuesday.
DAY TIME INDICATOR PERIOD AVG F/CAST PREVIOUS
Thu 2245 a Merchandise trade May $293.5 million $55.3 million
b Merchandise trade Yr to May -$563.3 million -$541.1 million
Thu 0200 c Govt surplus* 1997/98 $2.23 bln n/a
d GDP growth Mar 98 yr 1.90 pct n/a
e Treasury f/c GDP Mar 98 yr 2.58 pct n/a
f GDP growth Mar 99 yr 3.18 pct n/a
g Treasury f/c GDP Mar 99 yr 3.66 pct n/a
Further information:
FORECAST NO OF RESPONDENTS MEDIAN RANGE
a Eight $312.5 million $160 to $400 million
b Eight -$546.5 million -$708 to -$431 million
c Nine $2.0 bln $1.6 to $2.9 bln
d Five 1.7 pct 1.6 to 2.3 pct
e Five 2.5 pct 2.5 to 2.9 pct
f Five 3.1 pct 2.8 to 3.2 pct
g Five 3.5 pct 3.5 to 4.0 pct

BUDGET: * Government surplus forecasts were mainly polled and gathered prior to Winston Peters' Friday comment that market forecasts were over-optimistic. On tax cuts, the nine economists surveyed by Reuters were unanimous that the government tax cuts scheduled for July 1998 would still be implemented.
Respondents to the survey were: ANZ Bank, ASB Bank, Bankers Trust NZ, Bank of New Zealand, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, Doyle Paterson Brown, Garlick and Co, National Bank of New Zealand, SBC Warburg.
